decision: v0.1 uses versioned atomic local JSON manifests rather than an embedded database

invariants: segments are contiguous and every completed offset is within its inclusive range
segment coverage equals known total bytes
completed manifests have every segment fully complete
only HTTP(S) URLs without embedded credentials are accepted

migrationPlan.strategy: reject unknown versions without rewriting them; future upgrades create and validate a backup before write-new-and-swap migration
migrationPlan.rollback: restore the validated pre-migration manifest and retain the rejected source for diagnosis

implementation: restore_manifest validates before replacing live state
live writes retain a previous copy until the new manifest is installed
backupRestorePlan.scope: metadata only; downloaded content and partial bytes remain destination filesystem assets
backupRestorePlan.recovery: active state loads as recoverably_interrupted and preserves per-segment completed offsets

indexPlan.reason: one manifest per download is addressed by its known path; v0.1 has no database scan or measured query requiring an index
indexPlan.futureTrigger: add a rebuildable index only after retained-history query measurements justify it

capacityPlan.metadataComplexity: O(segment count), bounded to eight segments by the transfer engine
capacityPlan.headroom: a manifest update can temporarily require live plus temporary plus previous metadata copies
capacityPlan.contentBudget: destination capacity must cover the expected download bytes; content is not duplicated into metadata backups

evidence: persistence remains in the shared download-engine crate
exact cargo test and diff-check commands are reported by WS-06; disposition remains reserved for ENG-15

implementationNotes: Persistence, validation, backup, restore, and recovery rules are implemented once in packages/download-engine and are available to UI adapters through the shared crate.
No production services, credentials, database operations, or deployment are involved.
knownRisks: Metadata and destination file bytes cannot share one filesystem transaction.
Power loss and filesystems without durable rename semantics still require startup reconciliation and Windows fault-injection coverage.
Manifest URL and output path are sensitive local metadata and backups inherit the same access requirements.
Independent verification remains reserved for ENG-15.
